newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Editorials - Oct 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Editorials - Oct 15.

text.p: NOTE: These are highlights of comments in the Hong Kong press. The views expressed are those of the newspapers quoted, and do not represent an editorial viewpoint of Reuters.

- With 259 days to go before the British colony reverts to China, editorials in the Hong Kong media concentrated on a letter threatening to gas people in the Hong Kong Mass Transit Railway and on Chinese dissidents Wang Dan and Wang Xizhe.

-- MING PAO DAILY NEWS said that the public should not panic over the gas threat, because that was exactly what terrorists want. It said when the Diaoyu Islands protesters forced their way into the Japanese consulate, they brought violence to the originally peaceful movement. Many overseas media might think that was the cause of the gas threat and their understanding and support of Hong Kong would be qualified. It said people should be aware that irresponsible actions might cause huge damage to Hong Kong.

-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC TIMES asked how the future chief executive would handle cases involving Chinese dissidents after the handover, saying there were not many options. If Beijing insisted on Hong Kong repatriating any illegal immigrants, the Special Administrative Region government of Hong Kong would have to obey. But Beijing's basic attitude towards dissidents was to get rid of trouble and the easiest way was to send them overseas. So the future chief executive had to be practical and know how the Chinese leaders think, while a weak chief executive might rush to demonstrate his or her loyalty by repatriating the dissidents immediately.

-- The English-language HONGKONG STANDARD said that it was not too late for the Preparatory Committee to draw up a set of guidelines for the registration for the post of chief executive to avoid chaos. It said it would be better if the Selection Committee demonstrated transparency and fairness than simply throw the application process open to all.
